entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-93qh-vwrm-c5pw: Jenkins: Stored XSS vulnerability in node offline cause description
entry.content:
Jenkins: Stored XSS vulnerability in node offline cause description

Aliases: BIT-jenkins-2026-53441, CVE-2026-53441

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • org.jenkins-ci.main:jenkins-core — fixed in 2.568

Jenkins 2.483 through 2.567 (both inclusive), LTS 2.492.1 through 2.555.2 (both inclusive) does not escape the user-provided description of a generic offline cause that could be set through the `POST config.xml` API, resulting in a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exploitable by attackers with Agent/Configure permission.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-386j-6m86-78f9: OpenAM: Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via RADIUS Spoofing
entry.content:
OpenAM: Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via RADIUS Spoofing

Aliases: CVE-2026-46560

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • org.openidentityplatform.openam:openam-radius — fixed in 16.1.1

## Summary **Description** An Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature (CWE-347) issue in OpenAM's RADIUS authentication module allows an unauthenticated network attacker to spoof an Access-Accept response and obtain an OpenAM session for any RADIUS username, without knowing the configured shared secret. This affects OpenAM Community Edition through version 16.0.6 and was patched in version 16.1.1. The RADIUS client opens an unconnected datagram socket and treats the first UDP datagram delivered to its source port as authoritative. The receive path does not check the source IP/port, does not match the response identifier to the outstanding request, and does not verify the Response Authenticator (RFC 2865 §3); the RFC 2869 Message-Authenticator is neither sent nor required. Under certain conditions, this may allow an attacker to forge OAuth2 bearer tokens and OIDC ID tokens with arbitrary subject, client, realm, and scope. entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-hgj6-7826-r7m5: jackson-databind: InetSocketAddress deserialization triggers eager DNS resolution (SSRF)
entry.content:
jackson-databind: InetSocketAddress deserialization triggers eager DNS resolution (SSRF)

Aliases: CVE-2026-54514

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 2.18.8
  • com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 2.21.4
  • com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 3.1.4
  • tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 2.21.4
  • tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 3.1.4

## Summary `JDKFromStringDeserializer` constructed `InetSocketAddress` with `new InetSocketAddress(host, port)`, which performs eager DNS name resolution for hostname inputs at deserialization time. An application that binds untrusted JSON into a type containing an `InetSocketAddress` field issues an attacker-chosen DNS query during `readValue`, before any application-level validation or connect logic. The fix uses `InetSocketAddress.createUnresolved(host, port)`, deferring DNS to an explicit connect. ## Impact An attacker controlling JSON deserialized into an `InetSocketAddress`-bearing type can force outbound DNS lookups for attacker-chosen hostnames at deserialization time (SSRF / DNS-based out-of-band interaction / internal-resolver probing), purely from binding. ## Affected / Patche…

entry.content:
jackson-databind's renamed @JsonIgnore'd setters can deserialize via private fields

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N

## Summary `POJOPropertiesCollector._renameProperties()` allows a property with `@JsonProperty("renamed")` on the getter and `@JsonIgnore` on the setter to be renamed rather than dropped. entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-rmj7-2vxq-3g9f: jackson-databind has an array subtype allowlist bypass in BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator (allowIfSubTypeIsArray)

jackson-databind has an array subtype allowlist bypass in BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator (allowIfSubTypeIsArray)

Aliases: CVE-2026-54513

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

## Summary `BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator.Builder.allowIfSubTypeIsArray()` allowlists any array type based only on `clazz.isArray()`, without validating the array's component (element) type against the configured allowlist. entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-j3rv-43j4-c7qm: jackson-databind has a PolymorphicTypeValidator bypass via generic type parameters that allows arbitrary class instantiation
entry.content:
jackson-databind has a PolymorphicTypeValidator bypass via generic type parameters that allows arbitrary class instantiation

Aliases: CVE-2026-54512

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 2.18.8
  • com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 3.1.4
  • com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 2.21.4
  • tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 3.1.4

`jackson-databind`'s `PolymorphicTypeValidator` (PTV) is the primary safety mechanism guarding polymorphic deserialization. When polymorphic typing is enabled and a type identifier contains generic parameters (i.e. the type ID string contains `<`), `DatabindContext._resolveAndValidateGeneric()` validates **only the raw container class name** (the substring before `<`) against the configured PTV. If the container type is approved, the method parses the full canonical type string via `TypeFactory.constructFromCanonical()` and returns the fully parameterized type **without ever validating the nested type arguments** against the PTV. The nested type arguments are then resolved, instantiated, and populated as beans during deserialization. An attacker who controls the type ID can therefore pla…

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N/E:H

  • components/jquery — fixed in 3.5.0

### Impact Passing HTML containing `<option>` elements from untrusted sources - even after sanitizing them - to one of jQuery's DOM manipulation methods (i.e. `.html()`, `.append()`, and others) may execute untrusted code. ### Patches This problem is patched in jQuery 3.5.0. ### Workarounds To workaround this issue without upgrading, use [DOMPurify](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify) with its `SAFE_FOR_JQUERY` option to sanitize the HTML string before passing it to a jQuery method. ### References https://blog.jquery.com/2020/04/10/jquery-3-5-0-released/ ### For more information If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, search for a relevant issue in [the jQuery repo](https://github.com/jquery/jquery/issues). If you don't find an answer, open a new issue.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-r6fj-869h-4f6q: OHttpVersionChunkDraft: Missing Final-Chunk Enforcement Leads to Undetected Stream Truncation
entry.content:
OHttpVersionChunkDraft: Missing Final-Chunk Enforcement Leads to Undetected Stream Truncation

Aliases: CVE-2026-48480

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:U

Affected:

  • io.netty.incubator:netty-incubator-codec-ohttp — fixed in 0.0.22.Final

The codec-ohttp implementation of draft-ietf-ohai-chunked-ohttp does not verify that a cryptographically-signed final chunk was received before the outer HTTP body terminates. An on-path adversary (the OHTTP relay itself, or any MITM on the relay↔gateway or relay↔client transport) can forward a prefix of a legitimate chunked-OHTTP message—cut at a non-final chunk boundary—and close the outer body cleanly, producing no decryption error and no exception in the receiving application.

jackson-databind has case-insensitive deserialization bypasses per-property @JsonIgnoreProperties

Aliases: CVE-2026-54515

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N

  • com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 2.18.9
  • com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 2.21.5

## Summary In `BeanDeserializerBase.createContextual()`, per-property `@JsonIgnoreProperties` exclusions are applied by `_handleByNameInclusion()`, producing a `contextual` deserializer whose `BeanPropertyMap` has the ignored properties removed. The subsequent per-property case-insensitivity block (triggered by `@JsonFormat(ACCEPT_CASE_INSENSITIVE_PROPERTIES)`) rebuilds from `this._beanProperties` (the original, unfiltered map) instead of `contextual._beanProperties`, then overwrites the filtered map — restoring every property `_handleByNameInclusion` had just removed. entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-3wrr-7qpf-2prh: jackson-databind: Deeply nested JsonNode throws StackOverflowError for toString()
entry.content:
jackson-databind: Deeply nested JsonNode throws StackOverflowError for toString()

Aliases: CVE-2026-50193

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 2.14.0

### Impact Potential Denial-of-Service when attacker sends deeply nested JSON if (and only if) service: 1. Reads deeply nested (1000s of levels) JSON as `JsonNode` (ObjectMapper.readTree()) 2. Writes out same (or modifided) node using `JsonNode.toString()` which can consume significant amount of resources with concurrent relatively small requests (1000 nested arrays is 2kB). ### Patches Fixed in 2.14.0 via https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson-databind/issues/3447. ### Workarounds Avoid serializing `JsonNode` using `toString()`: use ObjectMapper.writeValueAsString(node)
